proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched cone-testing radii n^(-1/4)(log n)^(1/8) with unknown propensity and (log n/n)^(1/3) with supplied propensity, including a lawful flat-null mixture and hard-support converse transfer. The math panel passed, but the final novelty review assessed subfield below the field floor because of the fixed smoothness/model scope, exponent overlap, and tests inactive below 2^1024. Formalization was not started; the duplicate headline remains an editorial finding, and the reviewed informal artifacts are preserved for a possible re-anchor.
tldr: On the fixed observed-law class \(\mathcal M\), the conditional mean causal-effect monotonicity radius is proved to have order \(n^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/8}\) with unknown propensity and order \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) when the same propensity function is supplied. Writing \(L_n=\lceil\log_2(80n)\rceil\), the exact guarantees are \(cr(n)\le\rho_\star(n)\le Cr(n)\) and \(cs(n)\le\rho_\star^e(n)\le Cs(n)\), with \(r(n)=(L_n/n^2)^{1/8}\), \(s(n)=(L_n/n)^{1/3}\), \(c=2^{-30}\), \(C=512\), and \(n_0=2^{1024}\). Both attaining tests are total finite algorithms with full-null size at most \(0.05\) at every sample size. Fixed-sample occupancy and an all-size connected-component likelihood comparison certify the matching exactly-\(n\)-observation converses. The ratio of the two critical radii diverges at order \(n^{1/12}(\log n)^{-5/24}\). Converse guarantees also transfer to any testing class containing the corresponding finite hard support; the attaining upper guarantees remain specific to \(\mathcal M\).
gap: Hsu, Huber, Lee, and Liu \cite{HsuHuberLeeLiu2026} address continuous-dose mean-outcome ordering with asymptotic Cram\'{e}r--von Mises/DML inference. Their result, pointwise CATE minimax theory, and Gaussian regression monotonicity testing do not supply a finite-sample minimax radius for covariate-indexed binary-treatment CATE on the stated primitive rough-nuisance class. The unresolved steps are a lawful full-support cone-null converse, observational full-null calibration, and the unknown-location penalty.
fill: A finite original-data pair scan and null-supported fixed-sample likelihood comparison must jointly determine the unknown-propensity radius; a bounded-score scan and common-propensity converse must determine its supplied-propensity counterpart. Matched upper and lower bounds must establish or refute the candidate orders \(n^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/8}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) and decide whether their critical-radius ratio diverges.
